name: PoE Reconciler (Blue Intelligence)
summary: Give it one maritime zone and it returns the zone's Ports of Entry, where a sailor may legally clear customs on arrival, each with a verdict, a 0-100 confidence score, its sources and an evidence tier (official government page, independent port registry, both or neither), plus a short brief for sailors.

run.install: backend/.venv/bin/pip install fastapi==0.110.1 httpx==0.28.1 pydantic==2.13.4 python-dotenv==1.2.3 uvicorn==0.25.0 filelock==3.32.3 pycountry==26.2.16
run.sample_mode: No credentials needed: without a .env, run.py turns on SAMPLE_MODE and the agents run on bundled real data.

agents.name: RunPipeline
agents.role: orchestrator; one run_id and one JSONL trace per run

agents.name: ZetarisAdapter
agents.role: reads candidate ports and the UN/LOCODE and World Port Index registries through Zetaris SQL; looks up stored official evidence; assigns evidence tiers

agents.name: HMemAgent
agents.role: recalls and remembers verdicts with the Meterless H-MEM engine

agents.name: EvaluatorAgent
agents.role: scores each port and decides pass, flag or retry

agents.name: NemotronJudge
agents.role: advisory critic: one Nemotron call per zone on the official evidence text; never writes a tier or a score; may trigger one research round

agents.name: ResearchAgent
agents.role: on retry, adds the official source H-MEM remembers for the port

agents.name: BriefingAgent
agents.role: writes the sailor-facing brief through Meterless Nightshift

zetaris.use: data layer: every run reads its ports and two independent registries through Zetaris SQL, with a timeout and a fallback to bundled fixtures

meterless_engine.use: verification memory across runs; ResearchAgent reuses a previously verified official source on retry

meterless_nightshift.use: primary model provider for the brief and the NemotronJudge critique; records the requested and the served model

nvidia_nemotron.use: served through Nightshift; the recorded live run requested nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b

data.name: Blue Intelligence Ports of Entry seed (1,169 ports)
NGA World Port Index (US Government, public domain)
